conflicts.description: Both specifications validate Kubernetes deployments and pod health. kubernetes-deployment-validation-exit-codes uses validate-local-deployment.sh, while playwright-validation-workflow uses validate-deployment-playwright.sh. Risk of duplication and inconsistent validation approaches.
conflicts.resolution: RESOLVED - Specifications serve different purposes: kubernetes-deployment-validation-exit-codes validates exit codes and failure detection, playwright-validation-workflow validates API endpoints with browser automation. No actual conflict.

conflicts.description: Both validate deployed infrastructure, but at different layers. rpc-api validates RPC API deployment, playwright-validation-workflow validates Activity API deployment. Complementary, not conflicting.
conflicts.resolution: SYNERGISTIC - Both specifications validate different services in the same cluster. Can be combined in comprehensive deployment validation pipeline.

conflicts.description: Both specifications use Playwright MCP for browser-based validation. playwright-validation-workflow uses it for API endpoint validation, dashboard-login-flow uses it for UI testing.
conflicts.resolution: COMPATIBLE - Both use the same Playwright MCP infrastructure. Shared dependency on Playwright MCP server availability. No conflict, but both require MCP server to be running.

sharedComponents.changeType: MINIMAL - Added reference to new Playwright validation script (1 line)
sharedComponents.recommendation: No refactoring needed. validate-activity-system.sh continues to provide basic validation, new script provides comprehensive Playwright validation.
Ensure Playwright MCP server is running before executing either validation. Consider adding MCP server health check to validation scripts.
All specifications assume access to Kubernetes cluster. No conflicts, but validation order matters: infrastructure validation → deployment validation → API validation → UI validation.
Use timestamp-based naming to avoid file conflicts. Current implementation already uses timestamps (ISO 8601 format).
No conflicts. This report is specific to playwright-validation-workflow. Other specifications use different report files.

potentialIssues.description: Multiple specifications depend on Playwright MCP server being running and accessible. If MCP server is down, both playwright-validation-workflow and dashboard-login-flow-e2e-validation will fail.
potentialIssues.mitigation: Add MCP server health check at the beginning of validation scripts. Document MCP server setup requirements in deployment documentation.

potentialIssues.description: validate-deployment-playwright.sh uses kubectl port-forward to localhost:8080. If another process is using port 8080, port-forward will fail.
potentialIssues.mitigation: Script should check if port 8080 is available before starting port-forward. Add cleanup logic to kill existing port-forwards on the same port.
potentialIssues.status: PARTIAL - Script includes cleanup on exit, but doesn't check for existing port usage

potentialIssues.description: Playwright validation assumes infrastructure is deployed and healthy. Running playwright-validation-workflow before deploying infrastructure will fail.
potentialIssues.mitigation: Document validation order in deployment workflow: 1) Deploy infrastructure, 2) Validate deployment (kubernetes-deployment-validation-exit-codes), 3) Validate APIs (playwright-validation-workflow), 4) Validate UI (dashboard-login-flow).
potentialIssues.status: MITIGATED - Documentation includes deployment workflow order

recommendations.recommendation: Create comprehensive deployment validation pipeline that orchestrates all validation specifications in correct order
recommendations.reason: Multiple validation specifications exist but no unified pipeline to execute them in sequence
recommendations.implementation: Create scripts/validate-deployment-complete.sh that calls all validation scripts in order with proper error handling

recommendations.recommendation: Add MCP server health check to validation scripts
recommendations.reason: Multiple scripts depend on Playwright MCP but don't verify it's available
recommendations.implementation: Add opencode mcp list check at beginning of scripts that use Playwright MCP

recommendations.recommendation: Standardize validation report formats across specifications
recommendations.reason: Different specifications use different report formats (markdown, JSON, text)
recommendations.implementation: Create common validation report template/schema that all specifications can use

impactAssessment.directImpact: LOW - New files added, minimal modifications to existing files
impactAssessment.transitiveImpact: LOW - No changes to core application code, only validation infrastructure
